title: Omri and His Dynasty
lead: Omri (about 885–874 BC), an army commander who became king of Israel, built Samaria and founded the dynasty of Ahab, Ahaziah and Joram. Kings gives him a few lines and a harsh verdict; Moabite and Assyrian inscriptions show him as one of the most powerful kings Israel had.

sections.b: The army proclaimed Omri king after Zimri's coup, and after a civil war with Tibni he reigned twelve years, moving the capital from Tirzah to the hill of Samaria, which he bought (1 Kings 16:15–28). His son Ahab married Jezebel of Tyre and promoted Baal (1 Kings 16:29–33), and the dynasty ended when Jehu killed Joram and Jezebel (2 Kings 9–10). Micah later says that "the rules of Omri are kept, and all the works of the house of Ahab" (Micah 6:16). The Mesha Stele of Moab says Omri "oppressed Moab many days" and occupied Medeba (compare 2 Kings 3:4–5). Assyrian kings called Israel "the house of Omri" for over a century, and Ahab fielded 2,000 chariots at Qarqar in 853 BC.
